pieces.title: East-West
pieces.dek: The gate read from its far side. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline — 1,200 km to Yanbu, about 4 million barrels a day rerouted since the Strait was constricted, about 4 percent of global supply — attacked again on Monday in the Medina region: a 'limited fire', no casualties, operations not affected, says the ministry that owns it; no attacker named, the Houthi war intensifying beneath it, the September shutdown the precedent. A pipeline is essential for bypassing the Strait only while the Strait is shut; the dek says the gate is shut without naming it. Beside the Fox page cut the same morning (the UAE's 4.4 million a day through Fujairah), roughly eight million barrels a day are going around the gate, and the route has become a theatre.

pieces.title: Month Eight
pieces.dek: The holder on the tape twice, as the shadow — 'the wars we never get into', 'the first president in decades who started no new wars' — put to Trump voters around Fort Bragg. The lowest line is a veteran who voted on the promise 'for just one reason': 'promised to never happen, then four weeks, then a couple months — now we're in month eight'. Nobody dates a strike; the force is read as its own length, the price touched three times and never sized; the one supporter who declines to read it is the tape's ceiling.
pieces.lede: LI · Dia 31 · declared +1.0 (Trump, clips) · read z −0.33 · Lumens 47 · 17 lines + 2 constitutive. The same corner, day and object as A Spine, a point higher and seven lumens dimmer — the difference is the promise in the holder's own voice rather than a voter's memory. Two open lines overlap with A Spine's lift; both cuts say so. Cut 11-01 from the 10-30 sweep on its second day as the queue (no 10-31 or 11-01 sweep reached GitHub).

pieces.title: Win or Come Home
pieces.dek: The record in one reported clause — 'moves are underway to give the president options if he resumes strikes' — in the same paragraph as the vice-president's 'not going to let Iran become a forever war'. A House Armed Services Republican answers with a binary, asks for Congress 'if he renews military action', and then describes coming home: 'over the horizon monitoring' and strikes to 'mow the lawn every now and again'. No price, deal or Strait on the page; 'economic stability' once.
pieces.lede: RI (proposed) · Dia 30 · declared +0.8 (Vance) · read z −0.30 · Lumens 46 · 12 lines + 1 constitutive. The first Fox read of the force rather than the price, and the first war-powers stop asked for from inside the majority. The force now read from three corners in three cutting days, every read below zero; the only voice above it is constitutive. Cut 11-01 from the 10-30 sweep on its second day as the queue; Vance @O and 'mow the lawn' as O are Claude's calls — rulings owed.

pieces.title: The Linchpin
pieces.dek: The terminal on the Friday before the vote: WTI $104, 'the highest levels since near the beginning of the war'; the price measured where it lands — Exxon's refining a record $9.05bn, almost five times a year earlier, Chevron's nearly $5bn, four times, 'international prices are up 60%'; the cause named three ways — the Strait 'a little more challenging', strikes 'after the midterm elections', 'Russia–Ukraine, because diesel has been the linchpin'. The deal is never named; the holder's only instrument on the tape is 'that Truth Social post'.
pieces.lede: RI · Dia 16 · declared — · read z −0.53 · Lumens 82 · 26 lines, register-touching segments of a 2:24 program. The RI corner's first non-Fox read of H1c and the first with the cause on the tape: Fox 10-29 read the same price with the cause removed. Chevron's Venezuelan barrels 'cost less than $20' against crude 'north of $100' — the renamed cure read as the seller's margin. The Fed's December meeting is the market's substitute clock, refused once (Golub: the rate 'is not going to affect inflation coming out of oil in the Middle East'). First Surveillance cut. Cut 10-31 from the 10-30 sweep.

pieces.title: A Spine
pieces.dek: The LI corner reads the force through a Senate candidate on the Friday before the vote: 'the president now reportedly plans to re-up strikes against Iran as soon as the midterms are over' (the host, the lowest line), a senator briefed on the plan ('insane'), and Dan Osborn's answer — the Senate as the stop — with the sentence no corner had said: Russia 'supported Iran in this war that has killed Americans — and now we're doing a diesel deal with Russia'. Two Fort Bragg voters open it with the promise: 'he should keep his promises — no wars'.
pieces.lede: LI · Dia 30 · declared — · read z −0.40 · Lumens 54 · 15 lines. The deal and the war it is meant to cure in one sentence, from a slate candidate (NE-Sen). Osborn oscillates inside one sitting — 22–30 on mechanisms, 54–58 on the country. Ten lower and sixteen brighter than the corner's last read of the war (10-21). Cut 10-31 from the 10-30 sweep; the NC voters' clip (ms-now 10-30) filed, not cut.

pieces.title: Five Options
pieces.dek: A beta lede of the RP strategist's menu — five options on Iran after the vote; hed, dek and the two least escalatory options visible. The clock is the vote's, and the page says why: escalation now 'would spook the financial markets and harm Republican candidates next Tuesday'. The deal is priced in the Strait — Iran's terms (lift the blockade, sanctions relief, recognize Iranian control), a June memorandum recognizing Iranian sovereignty in the strait that collapsed in under two weeks, and a quick deal that would 'surrender the strait'. Transits 'appear to have restored … near pre-war levels'.
pieces.lede: RP · β · Dia 21 · declared — · read z −0.51 · Lumens 61 · 11 lines · depth 0.27. The corner's third page on the force in three days (Gur, Doran, MacLean) and the first whose visible text reaches the Strait and a dated record. Runs as data, not in the corner's figure. Cut 10-31 from the 10-30 sweep; nothing fuller in RP.

pieces.title: Little Surprise
pieces.dek: The deal's price leg at the index: September PCE +0.5% on the month, +3.6% on the year from 3.4%, core 3.1%, the savings rate down to 3.8%. The page reads the number against a forecast ('little surprise', 'stubborn') and sorts it into the Fed's December meeting — a hike at 79.6%. The only cause on the page is a guest's clause, 'as oil prices spike'. Gasoline, the pump, the war, the deal and the holder's clock are absent; the AP wire's reading of the same release — gas drove it, oil above $100 — is on PBS, filed as the record, not here.
pieces.lede: RI (proposed) · Dia 22 · declared — · read z −0.21 · Lumens 60 · 17 lines. The most fluid Fox read of the deal's price and the one with the least of the object on it: eleven dated numbers, one cause, the Fed's clock in place of the holder's. Method-occluded — the first piece on the Press carrying that mode. Seventh RI read in twelve days, all Fox, none above zero. Cut 10-30 from the 10-29 sweep (no 10-30 sweep at run time).

pieces.title: Go From Here
pieces.dek: A beta lede of the Israel correspondent's post-election essay — headline, dek and five paragraphs to the wall. The dek reads the result (53 / 48 / 19 of 120, none at 61) as 'just well enough for his highest priority: bringing down the Iranian regime'; the body is the Knesset's arithmetic. The object appears once, in the dek, undated, with no order; the light that gets through is the seat count's.
pieces.lede: RP · β · Dia 29 · declared — · read z −0.07 · Lumens 43 · 8 lines · depth 0.25. The corner's second page on the force in two days (Gur 10-28: the vote as the enabler; Doran 10-29: the strike as inevitable), neither dated. The LP reads of the same object (Breaking Points 10-28, 10-29) are on the queue with no transcript. Runs as data, not in the corner's figure. Cut 10-30 from the 10-29 sweep.

pieces.title: What to Plant
pieces.dek: Diesel as a buyer's number for the first time on the Press: 72% over an Arkansas extension budget across the seasons, urea 39% over, the Strait's closure named as the spring cause, $343m of added cost for one state, bankruptcies up 73% on two years. The holder's answer on the page is cash — the $8bn fuel relief program, which the article sizes at under half of the one state's bill. The deal is not on the page; the buyer's answers are a crop plan (rice to soya) and a vote.
pieces.lede: LI (non-US horizon) · Dia 22 · declared — · read z −0.24 · Lumens 52 · 25 lines. The two legs of H1c on one day from two corners: the Texas pump on Fox, the Arkansas field here, the deal on neither. The sweep matched this page on 'midterm' only — the feed carries no body text — and never saw the diesel line; found by reading. Cut 10-29 from the 10-29 sweep.

pieces.title: The Long Haul
pieces.dek: The Georgia page from Texas, five days on, with the pump gone national — regular $4.25 against $3.05 a year ago, up nearly 40% — the holder's clock at its fifth and fastest phrasing ('really fast', 'very, very rapidly'), and the cure renamed: not Russian diesel but Venezuelan oil, a million barrels 'free' and refined in Texas, with the administration's own clock for it at 'eventually'. Four clocks on one page for one price; the voters grant the number and move the threat to the republic.
pieces.lede: RI (proposed) · Dia 33 · declared +0.9 (Trump) · read z −0.04 · Lumens 25 · 17 lines + 2 constitutive. The sixth RI read of the deal's price in eleven days, all from Fox, none above zero — and the first in which the cure beside the pump is not the one the deal was for. Cut 10-29 from the 10-29 sweep; the Venezuela deal scored as H1's cure renamed by Claude's call — ruling owed.

pieces.title: Inevitable
pieces.dek: A beta lede of a podcast page — headline, dek and one teaser paragraph that stops mid-word. The hed calls another Iran strike inevitable; the dek calls it a prospect and the deal a question; the paragraph asks whether Iran costs Republicans the midterms and promises a swipe at Tucker Carlson. Five lines, none touching the record: Lumens 0, the first on the Press; depth 0.2, the lowest.
pieces.lede: RP · β · Dia 40 · declared — · read z −0.22 · Lumens 0 · 5 lines · depth 0.2. The RP corner's newest word on the force, from the author of the 10-13 diesel lede; runs as data, not in the corner's figure. Cut as a beta because the corner had nothing fuller today — a ruling owed on whether a one-paragraph teaser is a lede at all.

pieces.title: Eyes to the Sky
pieces.dek: The Strait from the force's side, read from Tehran's street: the page never names the water, only the lock on it — the naval blockade of Iran's southern ports since July, oil exports halted, which the holder threatens to prolong — and the clock: strikes after the two elections, the military ready 'in the coming days if ordered', energy facilities promised by Israel's defence minister. Two residents and an X user wait for the jets; nobody on the page expects the water to open.
pieces.lede: LI (non-US horizon) · Dia 26 · declared z −0.7 (Trump, the force's holder, on this axis) · read z −0.36 · Lumens 38 · 22 lines + 2 constitutive. The holder's 'U.S. control' (10-11) reopened the water; his reported sentence here keeps it shut — one hand, two sentences. The price read from the other shore (incomes cut by the blockade) the day after Georgia's pump (up on Iranian attacks): each page names the other side's hand. Cut 10-28 from the 10-27 sweep (no 10-28 sweep at run time); scored as H6 with the Strait unnamed by Claude's call — ruling owed.

pieces.title: Two Electorates
pieces.dek: The price as the RI corner's own pollster counts its audience seven days out: gas prices a top-four issue tied to Iran (83%), Democrats preferred on it by twelve, approval 44 → 36 since the war. No price, no diesel, no Strait, no deal on the page — the gas↔votes predicate measured for the first time from the corner paying, and the rest a map: Texas 49–49, Ohio to Lean D, the Senate 48/47, the House floor 223.
pieces.lede: RI (proposed) · Dia 18 · declared — (no holder on the page) · read z −0.11 · Lumens 47 · 23 lines, one voice. The lowest Fox figure of the week; the fifth RI read of the deal's price in nine days, all from Fox, none above zero. The holder's 'soon' (10-24) given seven days by his own corner's poll. Cut 10-28 from the 10-27 sweep. Station flagged; ten slate lines kept as vacancy — rulings owed.

pieces.title: Who Breaks First
pieces.dek: The Strait from Tehran's side: the page gives Iran the leverage and the control, puts reopening behind a four-item price list from the Supreme National Security Council — sanctions, assets, the blockade, assurances, 'only after' — and records October as the worst month for attacks on shipping, Brent above $117 on Iranian tanker attacks. A reopening was agreed once in June and failed in July.
pieces.lede: LI (non-US horizon) · Dia 23 · declared z −0.8 (Rezaei, the Strait's holder on the page) · read z −0.40 · Lumens 45 · 35 lines + 2 constitutive. The first LI page this week to name the restrictor; the holder's 'U.S. control' on no line. The force's two clocks marked (November 3; Tuesday's vote in Israel). Rezaei made the principal by Claude's call — the Enrollment Ruling applied to the other side; ruling owed.

pieces.title: Give Him Time
pieces.dek: One price on the page and it is a dollar up: Georgia gasoline $3.66 against $2.72 in February, with Iranian attacks on shipping as the article's cause. The holder's sentence at the rally has shortened to 'oil prices will come down soon' — no deal, no Strait, no diesel in it — and the voters read the gap as time: give him time, temporarily, worth paying.
pieces.lede: RI (station proposed) · Dia 33 · declared z +0.9 · read z −0.03 · Lumens 29 · 16 lines. The widest declared/read gap on the Press this week; the article checks the holder's 1.7% against the BLS's 3.7%. Two fuels now on the record from one network in four days — diesel above $6, gasoline $3.66 — and no page with both. Chosen over the Port Huron rally page and the Bessent page by Claude's call; ruling owed.

pieces.title: Paying the Price, in Euros
pieces.dek: The same price from the other side of the water: Europe's diesel doubled, its fossil-fuel import bill up €106bn, Brent above $100 since spring. The deal is on the page once — Washington asking Europe to open its emergency diesel stocks and take Russian diesel back. The Commission president's own migration: 'renewed hope' in February, 'paying the price' on October 16.
pieces.lede: LI (non-US horizon) · Dia 28 · declared z — (no holder on the page) · read z −0.32 · Lumens 50 · 24 lines. H1c read from Europe, with the Strait and the next strike marked. Two corners read the same cargo the same day from opposite sides: RI sizes it at a couple of hours; the non-US corner does not size it at all. Chosen over the day's CENTCOM explainer by Claude's call; ruling owed.

pieces.title: A Couple of Hours
pieces.dek: The first tanker is at sea — 40,000 tons for New York — and the pump is above $6 the week it sails. The holder's schedule is on the page in capitals (300,000 tons immediately; prices 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST'); the page's one reader sizes the cargo at a couple of hours of American demand, which is the wire's seven percent of a day said another way.
pieces.lede: RI (station proposed) · Dia 22 · declared z +0.95 · read z −0.20 · Lumens 62 · 10 lines. The cargo's third sighting (AJ 10-21 → AP 10-23 → Fox 10-24); the first Press sighting of the pump above six. Trump @O as the holder, Peskov @O as the seller ('regular supplies will continue'). The article sits at the floor; the general lifts the page alone. Chosen over the day's blockade page by Claude's call; ruling owed.

pieces.title: Eight Ministers, One Strait
pieces.dek: Eight foreign ministers meet in Istanbul about the Strait of Hormuz and count zero of eight for another strike; the Italian wants dialogue 'to reopen Hormuz', the R4 want 'full resumption of secure passage'. The same day a US envoy says Washington could 'absolutely' strike this weekend — and that the aim is not regime change.
pieces.lede: LI (non-US horizon) · Dia 20 · declared z +0.45 · read z −0.32 · Lumens 58 · 13 lines. Three corners now read the Strait as not open; the non-US corner is the mildest and the first to say 'reopen'. Two clocks on one page (the ministers', the strike's) and two principals naming two ends on consecutive days. Declared on H6 with the force marked — the reverse of the 10-22 cut; Claude's call, ruling owed.

pieces.title: Kept in Reserve
pieces.dek: Within a week of the deal's instrument being used — most of the Graham Act's new penalties waived, the Russian diesel restrictions eased — the law's Republican authors read the lever as set down: 86–11, 'beyond irresponsible'. The expert prices the diesel 'fairly marginal' and the waiver as the act that matters.
pieces.lede: RI (station proposed) · Dia 23 · declared z +0.7 · read z −0.36 · Lumens 58 · 23 lines. The RI corner's second reading of H1 is the deal's own party reading its legal leg. Trump @O as the waiver's holder, Wright @O as the easing's ('a carrot'). The wire has the first cargo at sea: 40,000 t, New York, due 11-07 — four days after the vote. Chosen over the day's newer Fox hit by Claude's call; ruling owed.

pieces.title: The Primary Objective, Priced
pieces.dek: Seven days before his own election, Netanyahu says toppling Iran's government remains the primary objective. The page prices every instrument it would take — airpower that degrades, a ground force nobody has offered, a partner that refused this week on timing — and finds each absent or unsigned.
pieces.lede: LI (non-US horizon) · Dia 16 · declared z +0.9 · read z −0.32 · Lumens 77 · 20 lines. The day's only full read on the force: the NYT's post-election strike plan mirrored by the FT's refused proposal. Two lines read the Strait (Iran's antiship stock; a strait Iran chooses not to close) and are marked. Scored on slate01's force by Claude's call; ruling owed.

pieces.title: The Word, Shrunk
pieces.dek: Jennifer Welch, on a clip Bad Faith plays, says she wishes she didn't have to use the word socialism. Briahna Joy Gray says what people like her mean by it is 'maybe we should have a little healthcare.'
pieces.lede: LP · Dia 37 (spread 14→62) · read z −0.33 · Lumens 40 · 11 lines. Gray 43 · Weber 44 · El-Sayed 22 · Welch 16. The left's fight over the word, two weeks before the midterms. Cut for The Parallelogram Report ep. 1.

pieces.title: One Tanker's Worth, Borrowed
pieces.dek: Twelve days after the deal said prices would come down, the Energy Department loans 315,000 barrels of distillate from the Northeast reserve — about 42,000 tonnes, one Russian tanker's worth — landing ten days after the election, to be returned with a premium. The page never mentions the deal.
pieces.lede: RI (station proposed) · Dia 14 · declared z +0.45 · read z −0.21 · Lumens 73 · 11 lines. The RI corner's first reading on H1 is a release notice that does not cite it: heating oil +70% on the year, +13% of New England supply, the cause named as the Iran War by a senator whose seat is on the slate. The tonnage arithmetic is the cut's.

pieces.title: The Only Voice of Reason
pieces.dek: “It shows how far we have fallen when Don Jr. is the only voice of reason within the administration.” The cable corner reads the Strait through the theater: the Fifth Fleet’s base at Bahrain, hit for $400 million; 21 killed, 865 wounded; eight months in.
pieces.lede: LI (cable) · Dia 40 · read z −0.55 · Lumens 38 · 17 lines. The hottest page since BP 10-12: the strategist and the general at 40–82, the Pentagon reporter at 10–22 with the record. Surface-bound — the corner never says Hormuz; it prices the base that holds it. Scored on H6 by Claude’s call; ruling owed.

pieces.title: The First Tanker, Sized
pieces.dek: Thirteen days after “immediately,” the first diesel tanker has a date: Thursday, 40,000 tonnes, port withheld. The wire restates the 300,000-tonne first tranche beside it and never divides. The Press does: thirteen percent.
pieces.lede: LI (non-US horizon) · Dia 10 · declared z +1.0 · read z +0.09 · Lumens 90 · 7 lines. A Reuters wire under the AJ masthead — the lowest-Dia reading on the deal. Novak and Witkoff speak for the deal’s two sides (“needing financing”); Ukraine’s MoD carries the challenge (half of Russia’s refining offline). Whether a wire reads as LI is a ruling owed.

pieces.title: Not Open for Business
pieces.dek: Two days into H6’s window, by Iran’s claim through Reuters, two tankers struck mines and one was left immobilized — the falsifier’s own words. The regulator says the one recognized route still has mines on it and the Strait is “not open for business in the way that it was.” CENTCOM, asked, did not answer.
pieces.lede: RI (station proposed) · Dia 16 · read z −0.56 · Lumens 73 · 19 lines. The first RI-corner page on the water: the IMO’s secretary-general at Dia 8–14, Iran’s officials at 20–34. Iran’s tolled corridor is now on the record from the right; the seven-day reopening proposal is a register candidate. Filed as a sighting of H6’s test, not a ruling on it.

pieces.title: Out of Ships
pieces.dek: The second LP reading on the Strait reads it through what passage loses, not what it costs: about 950 very large tankers in the world and a couple hit a day. If “open” means two of every ten ships get hit, at some point they run out of ships.
pieces.lede: LP · Dia 18 · read z −0.55 · Lumens 82 · 8 lines. Two layers no reader had put on H6 — the fleet and the repair yards — plus three buffers spent (China’s imports, the SPR, the PPI) and the gas-to-approval predicate for the third time. The split on H6 is now legible: the populist corners count hulls, the institutional lede counts barrels; both are true. RP is in the room and silent on the object.

pieces.title: The Crunch, Sapping
pieces.dek: The floor’s second Close point. Yesterday the desk passed the crunch through; today it logged the bite three times on the record — CPI at the fastest rate since April, energy with “secondary effects in core,” gasoline that “continues to sap consumer spending” — and the sign flipped.
pieces.lede: RI · Dia 11 · read z +0.12 · Lumens 83 · 13 lines. The trade lines (oil up 3.5%, the gainers, Exxon’s $7.8B refining quarter) pass it through; the record lines bite; they cancel just above zero. The deal entered the Close for the first time, attributed: “what President Trump saw as a remedy,” under “a potential block by Congress.” A sighting, not a reading. Rolling floor over two cuts: Dia 10 · Lumens 88.

pieces.title: A Car, Then a Senate Seat
pieces.dek: The flying Roadster becomes a ranking of economic systems — 'economic fascism' for China, 'communism sucks' for the rest — and then a reason the Republicans must hold the Senate.
pieces.lede: RI · Dia 53 (spread 20→80) · read z +0.81 · Lumens 22 · 15 lines. Two registers in one voice: the mechanism lines ≈30, the charge lines ≈70. Cut for The Parallelogram Report ep. 1.

pieces.title: The Windfall, Relocated
pieces.dek: “Trump’s treating it as our windfall because we get five million tons. It’s Putin’s windfall.” The deal delivers — to the seller. The Daily’s relocation, said in the cable register: the transform’s second specimen.
pieces.lede: LI (cable) · Dia 33 · read z −0.47 · Lumens 60 · 25 lines. The same corner as the Daily, thirteen Dia points hotter — the first measured spread inside a corner on the deal. Velshi carries the record ($6.32 diesel, the letter with Cornyn named, Ukraine striking again); Freeland, an adviser to Zelensky, carries the relocation and the paper’s hottest LI line (86).

pieces.title: Still Flowing, at a Price
pieces.dek: The first LI reading on H6 — the Strait as CENTCOM claims it. The headline credits the flow, the dek prices it, and the two trackers in the paragraphs disagree on the direction: TankerTrackers up on September, Kpler down.
pieces.lede: A beta lede: six paragraphs before the wall. Dia 16 · read z +0.1 · Lumens 85. Both trackers put October throughput at 10–12 million barrels a day — under H6’s own 15-million falsifier line, if the units match CENTCOM’s 19 million. They may not. Not a Diesel Index piece: a different object.

pieces.title: The Crunch, Booked
pieces.dek: Ten days after Odd Lots read the diesel crunch from an airline’s ticket, Bloomberg’s closing-bell hour read it from a trucker’s filing and the Fed’s print — and never once asked whether it could bite. J.B. Hunt’s top line grew twenty percent including fuel surcharges; loads grew eight and a half; the PPI ran at a four-year pace and retail ex gas did not move. Seventeen lines, none above Dia 16, every one on the pass-through side of Z.
pieces.lede: The first daily cut of The Close as the Press’s floor. Dia 8, Lumens 92: the register at its most fluid, posting the record in order and declining to assemble it — aligned mode, as the scan list predicted for Bloomberg programming. Aquino sets the test (trucking as the indicator of demand) and the trucking company answers it fifteen minutes later with volumes up; nobody on the tape joins the two sentences.

pieces.title: The Seat, Before It Pays
pieces.dek: The first press cut on a race. Three voices read Texas’s Senate seat nineteen days out — a left populist, a right populist and a forecaster — and all three lean the same way: it flips. They are two Dia points apart, the most even corner the Press has drawn, because a segment about polls is mostly numbers. The one line that leaves the race is the one that matters most to this paper: as gas prices rise, Trump’s approval falls, nearly one to one.
pieces.lede: Polling is weight here, never z: UT has Talarico +3, Fort Bend County +18 (≈+2 statewide), the RCP average +2 — those go to the register. What the cut scores is what the room believes: a flip at +0.32, the forecaster deliberately lower (‘a cloudy mirror, not an oracle’), the hosts higher. Ken Paxton is on the tape, leaked, naming his three disadvantages — trail, paid on November 3.

pieces.title: The Strait, Priced
pieces.dek: CENTCOM says nineteen million barrels came through the Strait on Monday. Breaking Points puts the other numbers next to it: a Singapore-flagged tanker on the bottom of the channel, more than twenty attacks, freight at $1.4 million a day against $100,000, Riyadh’s airport down from 134 aircraft to 38, five World Cup stadiums dropped — and one line that is the whole arc in miniature: countries are paying Iran for passage.
pieces.lede: Both populist corners read Z the same way — the Strait is not controlled — and differ only in distance: Saagar carries the record at Dia 8–20, Krystal’s frames run to 72. The quoted institutional voice, Biden’s energy envoy, says it at Dia 8: ‘I can say I control it, but it’s costing me.’ A new PG01 object opens here — the control claim, proposed H6 — and the deal, three days on, hardens from instrument to triage.

pieces.title: The Down Payment
pieces.dek: The first LI (US) full read of the deal — the whole episode, not a lede. The Times sizes the cargo against the buyer’s own day: less than one day of US consumption. Then it moves the object: not fuel to the pump but a down payment to Moscow, with no concession in return.
pieces.lede: Dia 20 · read z −0.34 · Lumens 72 · 39 lines. No split on Z; the Dia gap is host (frames, 24–40) against correspondent (record, 6–24). The same morning’s print lede read Dia 17 / z −0.49 — the first beta lede whose full read matched it. Transform proposed: relocation. The Diesel Index now has its LI member read in full; three corners say the deal does not deliver, and RI has still not spoken.

pieces.title: The Deal, Sized
pieces.dek: The first LI (US) voice on the deal, and the first piece a sweep surfaced rather than a scan. The Times reads the cargo as arithmetic: 300,000 tons for October is about 75,000 barrels a day, against 693,000 that Russia itself shipped a year ago and 809,000 the Gulf no longer sends. Won’t knock down prices, says the page; unlikely to lower them, says the feed. Same verdict, two modals.
pieces.lede: A beta lede: headline, dek and seven paragraphs before the paywall. Dia 17 — the lowest any non-floor corner has posted on the deal, because the lede is mostly barrels in one unit. Read z −0.49, the same sign as FP’s −0.3 and BP’s −0.73: three corners now say the deal does not deliver, and the only corner yet to speak is RI. Excluded from the Diesel Index composite until read in full; the one challenge line is Argus’s — the issue is still Hormuz.

pieces.title: The Deal, as an Embarrassment
pieces.dek: A lede cut — headline, dek and the five open paragraphs of Aaron MacLean’s column; the rest is behind the wall. The door is more denominated than the room: the headline and dek read Dia 46 (‘disastrous’, ‘desperate’, ‘embarrassing’); MacLean’s own paragraphs read 20, and carry the pledge against the record, diesel up fifty percent, and both causes of the crunch.
pieces.lede: The second right-populist voice on the deal, from the institutional side of that corner. Saagar read an instrument — jawboning the market before the midterms. The Free Press reads a failure of statecraft — a competence story, surface-bound. Same sign on Z (does not deliver), different plane. Depth 0.57: five distinct touches in seven lines; the lede says more than its title.

pieces.title: The Diesel Deal, Reduced
pieces.dek: Two presidential statements credited delivery before it happened — 300,000 tons of Russian diesel a month, and an energy ceasefire “effective immediately.” The record inside the window: a few percent of US supply, a statute that bars the cargo, and strikes by both sides within hours.
pieces.lede: The segment reads the gap correctly and then argues about why it exists. Saagar reads an instrument (jawboning, a pitch to the market before the midterms); Krystal reads the same gap as character, and over ten minutes migrates from the good-faith reading at 5:52 to its opposite at 15:35 — one voice, one object, Dia 28 to 86.

pieces.title: The Ceasefire, Explained From Outside
pieces.dek: The first left-institutional reading of the diesel deal the Press has found, and it comes from outside the country: an explainer with every fact in the right order — Kharkiv struck after the statement, Brent at $103, diesel at a record $6.52, the eight-step series from Biden’s ban to Friday’s 300,000 tonnes — organized around a different question: why does Trump keep changing his mind?
pieces.lede: Three readers on one page disagree on Z without the page noticing. Streeter reads the deal from the cargo (the Russian barrels won’t matter while the Gulf is shut, −0.27); Muraviev reads it from the negotiation (officials were talking in August; the posts are not the policy, +0.23); the article’s own voice nets to nothing — its record line says broken, its price line says believed. Dia 17 against a floor of 13: fluid, institutional, surface-bound — right domain, wrong plane.

pieces.title: The Crunch, Passed Through
pieces.dek: Eleven days before the diesel deal, the institutional register spent fifty-three minutes on the thing underneath it: the refined-products crunch. It sized the crunch in the price’s own units — the crack through $100, Singapore jet doubled, Russia out of the complex — and sized the other side in the same breath: TSA records, a surcharge at a quarter of the ticket, no dent. One line above Dia 33 in the whole tape.
pieces.lede: The Press’s first RI sample, and the baseline the populist cuts get compared against: Dia 13 against BP’s 46, Lumens 80 against 41. The station splits on Z without noticing — Kang’s price says the crunch bites, Weisenthal’s seat says it passes through — and Alloway states the falsifier once, as a conditional: “if we evolve into actual physical shortages.”

pieces.title: The Crunch, as a Design
pieces.dek: Three weeks before the diesel deal, the right-populist corner read the crunch and got the record right — 825 refineries on earth, seven hit in the Gulf, Russia at seven percent of the world’s diesel, Brent over 100 but not 300 while the product ran away, diesel at $6.50 — and then told you who meant it. The crunch, in this reading, isn’t a shock. It’s the point of the war.
pieces.lede: The first time the Press has had one object read from two corners. The Close (RI, Dia 8) read the crunch as a line item — surcharged, passed into the index, read z −0.44. Tucker Carlson (RP, Dia 35) read it as a bite — ‘beyond what most people can pay,’ read z +0.44. Same record, opposite sign on Z; neither corner knows the other exists, and the figure now has a diagonal.

pieces.title: The Word, With Its Weight

pieces.lede: RP · Dia 21 (spread 8→38) · read z −0.52 · Lumens 55 · 10 lines. Apffel climbs to 38 and comes back down to 24 the moment he defines the word. Cut for The Parallelogram Report ep. 1.
